We don't just need to recognise God; we must become the recognition itself. God's transcendence is navigated, in the immanence of experience, by Beauty, God's power of showing and telling, of seeing and being seen. Ever is it Beauty that changes Man's way. To become the recognition of God is to first and foremost become Beauty, both as the experience itself and the content of such an experience. Adjusting life to this standard is the praxical consequence of God's recognition; it becomes clearer than anything else that Beauty is the telos of Being, already achieved in every quanta of creation, always achieving itself in the boundless creating of Life that we call Time, and that Humanity's role as a "clearing for the Divine" is a moral charge to be conscious in the living of a beautiful life. Appreciation, the spirit of the cultivation of things, is both parent and child to Beauty. True appreciation is the end of Man; how can we appreciate that which has reached its own limit? Humanity is genuinely appreciable; as an openness for Beauty, Humanity is her canvas. Any great artist knows that Great Art simply "comes through", the means of making Per-fection.
